parties: Supreme Engineering Limited; Bank of India
headline: Supreme Engineering Limited announces one-time settlement with Bank of India
sum: Supreme Engineering Limited has entered into a one-time settlement (OTS) with Bank of India, formally announced to the NSE on 13 August 2026. The settlement resolves outstanding loan obligations between the company and the public-sector lender.
implication: OTS structures under RBI guidelines provide debt-stressed corporates a mechanism to cure defaults without triggering insolvency proceedings; the precedent here turns on the lender's willingness to take a haircut and the company's demonstrated ability to service remaining obligation—a marker of RBI-directed forbearance policy in action.
detail: Supreme Engineering Limited, an industrial equipment and engineering solutions provider, disclosed a one-time settlement arrangement with Bank of India via an NSE regulatory announcement on 13 August 2026. One-time settlements are debt-restructuring instruments used when a borrower facing liquidity stress or default risk reaches agreement with a lender to settle outstanding dues at a negotiated amount or terms, typically involving a partial write-off or extended repayment schedule. The announcement does not disclose the settlement amount, haircut percentage, or repayment timeline; these details are typically confidential between lender and borrower and may be disclosed only if material under SEBI's Listing Obligations & Disclosure Requirements (LODR).

framework.ref: RBI Master Direction – Non-Performing Assets (NPA) Classification and Management, 2021
framework.note: central; governs classification of advances as NPA and triggers for lender's forbearance and restructuring options, including OTS.

framework.ref: RBI Circular on Prudential Treatment of Standard Assets – Restructuring, 2020 (DBR.BP.BC.No.56/21.04.048/2019-20)
framework.note: central; sets out eligibility, provisioning and accounting norms for restructured advances; OTS is a variant of restructuring.

framework.ref: SEBI Listing Obligations & Disclosure Requirements (LODR) Regulation 2015, Reg. 30
framework.note: central; material event disclosure obligation; one-time settlements with lenders may require announcement if material to company valuation or financial condition.

framework.ref: Companies Act 2013, Section 179 (Directors' approval of borrowings)
framework.note: any refinancing or settlement of debt may trigger shareholders' approval thresholds depending on loan quantum.

framework.ref: Banking Regulation Act 1949, Section 45-L (Priority Sector Lending)
framework.note: if Bank of India classified the facility as priority-sector; OTS may trigger redeployment or slippage norms for the lender.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code 2016, Section 60 (Creditors' Settlement)
framework.note: OTS executed pre-IBC filing avoids formal insolvency moratorium and is faster; if post-default disclosure, lenders may face IBC-triggered claim scrutiny.

framework.ref: Income-tax Act 1961, Section 43(1) & Schedule VI (Bad-debt write-off deduction)
framework.note: lender's haircut component may qualify for bad-debt deduction if conditions met; borrower may have income/gain recognition on debt forgiveness.

framework.ref: RBI Guidelines on Fraudulent and Wilful Default, 2015
framework.note: if lender suspects wilful default, OTS may be blocked; OTS acceptance implies lender's satisfaction that default was not fraudulent.

conditions: Settlement amount / haircut percentage not disclosed in announcement
Repayment terms and timeline not disclosed
Likely conditions: completion of legal documentation, no material adverse change, adherence to revised repayment schedule
approvals: Bank of India internal credit committee approval (pre-announcement)
Supreme Engineering Limited board approval (likely, for debt restructuring)
structure.novel: No novel structure identified in public announcement; OTS is a standard forbearance tool under RBI policy.

triggers.note: triggers lender's right to offer OTS as alternative to formal restructuring or write-off; implies Supreme Engineering was classified NPA or 'standard but stressed.'
material event disclosure requirement if settlement quantum exceeds materiality threshold; NSE announcement fulfils disclosure obligation.
OTS avoids triggered insolvency filing; if loan is in default >180 days, lender's forbearance via OTS avoids threshold for creditor petition.

firms.note: Legal counsel not identified in the NSE announcement; Bank of India's in-house legal team likely coordinated with company counsel on OTS documentation.
